title: lockrot configuration
description: The `extra.lockrot` object in composer.json (config-2, lockrot 0.14). Unknown keys are allowed. Every config-1 document is config-2, except one that gives `ignore[].flags`, `accept-unchecked` or `advisory-lookup` a value that config-2 refuses. The listed keys must have the listed type. config-2 adds the `fail-on` list (a comma-separated string or a JSON array, one value per kind: a grade, a maintenance flag, a raw advisory severity, `unchecked`), `ignore[].flags`, `accept-unchecked` and `advisory-lookup`.

accept-unchecked.description: Checks that lockrot did not run and that the project accepts. Each entry names one check and one scope (`host`, `repository` or `package`), with a reason. It accepts exactly three gaps: a repository on a host that lockrot cannot ask (`host_not_supported`), a run whose Composer repositories publish no advisories (`no_feed`), and a package installed from vcs or from an origin that lockrot cannot tell (`not_from_composer_repository`). Every other unchecked reason stays S10, `undated_releases` included. An accepted check is not S10: `checks_skipped[]` lists it with the reason `accepted_by_config`, report-2 writes the entry in `finding.unchecked_accepted[]`, and `--fail-on=unchecked` does not fail on it. It hides no flag and changes no score. `ignore[]` comes first: a package that it accepts whole has no maintenance S10 left to accept. The first matching entry, in order, is the one that report-2 writes. lockrot 0.13 ignores this key.

check.description: The check that lockrot did not run: `repository_activity` (S3 and S4), `release_metadata` (S2 and S8) or `advisories` (S9). For a package outside every Composer repository, an accepted `release_metadata` also accepts the unknown fix of each counted advisory, because the fix scan reads the same releases. Its score can then be lower than with the releases read.

expires.description: A real calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). The entry accepts through 23:59:59 UTC that day, as an `ignore[]` entry does. lockrot rejects a date that does not exist, and this schema checks the shape. After that day the entry accepts nothing, and the check is S10 again.

host.description: The host of the repository URL of the package, as `finding.activity.host` writes it (`codeberg.org`, `git.example.com:8443`): lower case, with its port, without a scheme or a path. lockrot does not compare a GitLab path prefix of `activity.host`. Never with `check: advisories`: that gap comes from the Composer repositories, not from a source host.

package.description: The package name or a case-sensitive shell pattern (`acme/*`), matched with fnmatch as in `ignore[]`.

reason.description: Why the project accepts the check. report-2 shows it verbatim (`finding.unchecked_accepted[].accepted_by.reason`), never inside a machine string. lockrot rejects a reason of whitespace only.

repository.description: The repository that the package is installed from: its vcs URL (`https://github.com/acme/fork.git`, `git@github.com:acme/fork.git`), or the URL of a Composer repository (`https://mirror.acme.internal`). lockrot compares the lower-case host and the case-sensitive path, without the scheme, a trailing `/` or `.git`. A query and a fragment stay significant. A source URL matches on a host that lockrot cannot ask too. A Composer repository matches a package that lockrot attributes to it: by `origin.registry` when lockrot names the registry, else by the URL of the repository that lockrot read the entry from. The report does not write that URL. A package that lockrot cannot attribute to one repository never matches a Composer repository. A scheme URL carries no userinfo (lockrot rejects `https://user:secret@…` and `ssh://git@…`), because report-2 writes the value in `accepted_by.value` and a user name can be a token. Write `ssh://host:2222/path`: it matches the same source URL. Without a scheme lockrot reads only the scp form `user@host:path`. A `file://` URL has no host: accept such a package by `package`.

allOf.description: An entry with `check: advisories` cannot have `host`.

not.description: The advisories check is never scoped by host.

allOf.description: An entry needs exactly one of `host`, `repository` and `package`.

advisory-lookup.description: Which packages lockrot asks the advisory APIs of the Composer repositories about, by name. `all` (the default) asks every locked package, as `composer audit` does, so the name of a package installed from vcs, path or an archive reaches packagist.org. `composer-repositories` asks only the packages installed from a Composer repository, as 0.13 did, and marks every other one `checks_skipped` {check: advisories, reason: not_from_composer_repository}. `--offline` asks none.

baseline.description: The baseline file, relative to composer.json. lockrot 0.14 reads baseline-2 only; a baseline-1 file exits 2 until --generate-baseline overwrites it.

fail-on.description: When the run fails. `none` is the default and must stand alone. A grade (`critical high medium low`) fails when the band of the gate score is at or above it. A maintenance flag (`abandoned silent pinned left-behind old-promise stale capped`) fails on a counted flag at or above it in flag order that the baseline does not cover, as the verdict gate of 0.13 did. A raw advisory severity (`vulnerable`, `vulnerable-medium`, `vulnerable-high`, `vulnerable-critical`) fails on a counted advisory at or above it that the baseline does not know. `vulnerable` means any severity, so `vulnerable-low` is not a value. `unchecked` fails on S10. A list holds at most one value per kind. lockrot trims and lower-cases each value and accepts whitespace around commas. `--fail-on` and `LOCKROT_FAIL_ON` replace this value whole. This schema checks the spelling of each value. Two values of one kind and `none` beside another value are errors of lockrot itself (exit 2), which name the values. `run.fail_on` writes the list in canonical form.

allOf.description: `fail-on` is one value, a comma-separated list of values, or a non-empty array of distinct values.

oneOf.description: A comma-separated list in one string: `"high"`, `"left-behind, vulnerable-high"`.

allOf.description: A fail-on string is one value or a comma-separated list of values.

anyOf.description: One value, as an editor offers it.

oneOf.description: A JSON array, read as the string form is read: `["left-behind", "vulnerable-high"]`.

allOf.description: Each item is one fail-on value.

format.description: The output format. An open set in this published copy, so an editor holding it accepts a format a later release adds, or a `<vendor>:<name>` one; lockrot itself accepts exactly the formats in `x-known-values` of the copy it ships, and rejects any other as a configuration error.

expires.description: The date the entry stops accepting (`YYYY-MM-DD`). An expired entry accepts nothing and its flags count again.

flags.description: The maintenance flags that this entry accepts. Without it the entry accepts every maintenance flag, as in config-1. The other flags keep counting, and the repository activity lookup still runs unless the entry accepts every flag. A liveness word also accepts the liveness words below it. `vulnerable` is not a value: the allowlist accepts maintenance flags only. report-2 writes it as `finding.allowlist.flag_ids`. lockrot 0.13 reads an entry with `flags` as an entry that accepts the whole package.

package.description: The package name or a pattern with `*` wildcards (`symfony/*`).

reason.description: Why the project accepts it. Reports show it verbatim (report-2 `finding.allowlist.reason`, `reason_by: user`), never inside a machine string.

version.description: One exact version that the entry applies to. Without it the entry applies to every version.

ignore.description: The allowlist of the project: each entry accepts maintenance flags of the packages it matches, with a reason. An accepted flag is listed, muted, weighs 0 and reaches no gate. An entry never accepts an advisory. Accept advisories in the audit policy of Composer (`config.audit.ignore` on 2.4 to 2.9, `config.policy.advisories` on 2.10 and later), which `composer audit` reads too.

install-time.description: Whether the install-time pass runs after `composer install` and `update` (`on`, `off`).

install-time-budget.description: Seconds the install-time pass may take, 1–120 (default 5).

install-time-strict.description: Apply `fail-on` at install time and stop the transaction (https://lockrot.dev/install-time/#install-time-strict).

project.description: What a report should call this project, when the manifest's own name is not it — a package inside a monorepo, or a private project named after the client. Defaults to composer.json's own name. It renames the report's `run.project` only: it does not keep composer.json's name out of a report, whose `run.root_package` is always that name.

push-high-years.description: Years without a push or commit at which S4 reaches `high` (default 5).

push-warn-years.description: Years without a push or commit at which S4 reaches `warn` (default 3).

release-high-years.description: Years without a stable release at which S2 and S8 reach `high` (default 5).

release-warn-years.description: Years without a stable release at which S2 (no stable release) and S8 (none on the installed branch) reach `warn` (default 3).

target-php.description: The PHP minor the project runs on (`8.4`); the third link of the target chain.
